walkthroughs.body_html: Macbeth's soliloquy in Act 1 Scene 7 admits he has 'no spur to prick the sides of my intent, but only vaulting ambition'. Shakespeare presents ambition as a horse that throws its rider, leaping past its target. Every later horror grows from this admitted, unchecked drive.

The witches prophesy that Macbeth 'shalt be king', but never tell him to murder. Banquo hears the same prophecy and waits. The play asks whether prophecy plants a seed or merely sees one - and where personal responsibility begins.

After killing Duncan, Macbeth hears 'Macbeth shall sleep no more'. Lady Macbeth later sleepwalks, scrubbing imagined blood and crying 'Out, damned spot!' Shakespeare links conscience to the body - sleep, hands, blood - so guilt is not abstract but physically inescapable.
